messages:
Jason: Heads up — seeing repeated InsufficientResources for GPUs in us-central1-b. CA keeps provisioning in the same AZ and hits the GCE quota, so jobs queue. Can we fail traffic to another zone/cluster or prefer smaller GPUs automatically?

Kevin: hmm. sounds like CA is using the same node-group expander and not balancing. We can add soft-reservation nodegroups + taints to steer non-critical workloads. Also consider cross-zone fallback: prefer another zone in the same region first, then a different region.

Maria: +1. My rough plan: 1) make a `gpu-standby` nodepool with taint `gpu-standby=true:NoSchedule` that autoscaler can scale up from a different quota pool, 2) route lower-priority jobs there with tolerations, 3) fall back to quantized T4 instances for latency-tolerant jobs.

Kevin: example nodepool snippet I prototyped earlier:
```yaml
apiVersion: container.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: gpu-standby-us-central1-c
spec:
  initialNodeCount: 0
  config:
    labels:
      pool: gpu-standby
    taints:
      - key: "gpu-standby"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NO_SCHEDULE"
  autoscaling:
    minNodeCount: 0
    maxNodeCount: 8
```
Put tolerant jobs with tolerations like `tolerations: - key: "gpu-standby"`

sre-oncall: if we scale to another zone/region we need a traffic-routing plan. Latency-sensitive inference should not cross region. We need policy: prefer same-region other-zone first, then regional fallback for best-effort batch jobs only.

Jason: Agree. So policy = same-region cross-zone -> warm standby in sibling zone -> region fallback for non-critical. Also we should avoid provisioning the same instance family if quota is exhausted — try alternate families automatically.

infra-bot: alert: [2113456795] quota spike detected in us-central1-b: GPUs requested=120, available=16. Autoscaler event: "FailedScaleUp" x7.

Maria: On the autoscaler side, adjust flags: enable `--balance-similar-node-groups=true`, lower `--max-node-provision-time=7m`, and set `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` for better balancing. Also add `--expander=least-waste` for multi-nodegroup env.

Kevin: note on costs: cross-region fallback will cause egress + replication overhead (model snapshots, KV caches). For a 10k qps workload the egress hit could be non-trivial. Suggest we only permit cross-region for batch/async or after explicit approval.

Jason: For immediate mitigation I'm going to flip a quick staging patch to CA config and create the standby pool in staging:
```bash
kubectl apply -f ca-configmap-staging.yaml
kubectl apply -f nodepool-gpu-standby.yaml
```
I'll also open a short runbook draft: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-failover-draft (will link once created).

sre-oncall: please include a section: how to drain and preempt with minimal dropped requests and how to move KV cache warmers. Also add rollback steps if standby nodes blow budget.

Kevin: I'll run cost sims this afternoon comparing T4 vs A2 fallback and cross-region egress at 1%, 5%, 10% traffic shift. Will post numbers here.

Maria: Action items: 1) Jason patch CA + create `gpu-standby` in staging, 2) Kevin run cost sims and list acceptable thresholds, 3) SRE to draft routing policy and runbook. I'll coordinate a short Friday sync if needed.

Jason: 👍 starting patch now. Will update thread with `first-staging-rollout` timestamp.
